newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: U.N. urges return to democracy in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges return to democracy in Sierra Leone.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan called on Tuesday for the peaceful restoration of democracy in Sierra Leone and the country's U.N. envoy said he was confident that coup makers would be ousted soon.
Annan said the United Nations was not directly involved in negotiations to end the May 25 coup by junior military officers in Freetown or the command of the Nigerian-led military effort to oust them.
"There has been some fighting and attempts are still being made with the coup makers to get them to step down," Annan said.

"I hope that one would be able to find a way of resolving this situation, for the coup makers to leave and for the legitimate government to go back without much bloodshed," he told reporters at the Organisation of African Unity summit.
Sierra Leone's ambassador to the United Nations, James Jonah, said he had spoken to elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on Tuesday and remained confident that the coup would be over soon.

"If we were not concerned about reducing or eliminating civilian casualities I would see it over in a matter of days. But we want to avoid that and therefore we are going to use the most conservative means to remove them from power," he said.

Jonah said the Nigerian-led force that bombarded the city on Monday was strengthening its positions at two airports near the capital before beginning a final assault on the occupied government headquarters.
"When that is finished, they will go ahead with their objective, which is to remove these thugs who are parading as the government of Sierra Leone," he said.
